The slide introduces an approach based on an "efficient and flexible rendering pipeline" that renders image properties such as "occupancy", "depth", and "RGB" (Red, Green, Blue). Below this title, the text "Inverse Rendering with Neural Puppeteer" is displayed, which indicates the rendering process's inverse capability. The video segment presents a slide from a research presentation titled "Keypoint-Based Neural Rendering with NePu". The slide features a visual diagram showing the goal of the project, which is to "learn latent space that captures relations of 3D pose and image properties". It illustrates how ground truth (GT) keypoints and RGB-D images of a person in various poses are used as input to an encoder, which learns a latent variable (Z). This latent space captures the relationship between 3D keypoints and corresponding image properties such as RGB, silhouette, and depth. The presentation then transitions to describe the encoder architecture, mentioning PointTransformer[1] and AIR-Nets[2] for point cloud processing using attention mechanisms, along with a diagram showing the process of encoding keypoints into the latent variable Z, using a two-layer MLP with batch normalization and max pooling. The background of the slides is plain white with a logo of the University of Konstanz. Text at the bottom of the slide indicates the date of the presentation (07-12-22) and the title: "Neural Puppeteer: Keypoint-Based Neural Rendering of Dynamic Shapes".

The video segment presents a slide titled "Keypoint-Based Neural Rendering with NePu: Encoder," detailing the architecture of an encoder in a keypoint-based neural rendering system. The slide outlines "Step 1: Encode keypoints into latent variable z," illustrating the process with diagrams and text annotations. On either side of the word “encoder” are images of a 3D model of a person. Below this is a box called “encoder,” which contains a series of modules, including "VSA" (vector self-attention) followed by Batch Normalization ("BN"), then a "2-layer MLP", another "BN", "Linear" followed by "maxpool". To the right, the slide notes "Point Cloud Processing using Attention," mentioning PointTransformer and AIR-Nets as relevant techniques. The bottom of the slide includes citation information, the date "07-12-22," the title "Neural Puppeteer: Keypoint-Based Neural Rendering of Dynamic Shapes," and the University of Konstanz logo. In the next slide, the title changes to “Decoder,” and “Step2: Decode z into keypoints and local features,” with an accompanying schematic diagram showing the latent variable z being processed by MLPs and reshape operations to produce keypoints and features.

These key points are processed through an encoder and decoder to generate 3D key points and latent codes, which are then projected into 2D Keypoints. The diagrams show the flow of information. The video segment shows a presentation slide with the title "Synthetic Data" at the top. Below the title, there are bullet points listing the characteristics of the dataset, including approximately 900 to 5300 image instances per object, resolution of 0.3 to 4 Mpx, 19 to 33 keypoints per object, and 24 camera views. To the right of this list, there are four images featuring a cow, a giraffe, a pigeon, and a human figure. These appear to be renderings of these objects used to create the dataset. The next slide shows a title "Inverse Rendering with NePu", followed by a description and images of four silhouettes of a giraffe.
At the bottom of the slides, text reads "Neural Puppeteer: Keypoint-Based Neural Rendering of Dynamic Shapes" and "University of Konstanz", indicating the subject of the presentation and the affiliated institution, respectively. Additionally, "07-12-22" is displayed, which appears to be the date of the presentation. The information presented suggests that the narrator created a dataset of synthetic animals and people with specific characteristics such as resolution, keypoints and 3D locations.

The video segment showcases an academic presentation on "Inverse Rendering with NePu." The slides present a problem: multi-view silhouettes labeled as "Sc" with camera parameters "Ec, Kc." Four images in black and white depict the silhouettes of a horse in different poses. Additionally, text on the screen reads, "NePu learns a strong prior over distribution of z" which is followed by "Given: multi-view silhouettes Sc with camera parameters Ec, Kc". The slide later introduces a mathematical equation: "argmin over z of the sum for c equals 1 to capital C of BCE of SEc,Kc of dec(z), z, Sc, plus lambda times the double vertical bars z double vertical bars 2"  and the instruction "Obtain keypoint predictions by decoding z". The presentation originates from the University of Konstanz and is entitled "Neural Puppeteer: Keypoint-Based Neural Rendering of Dynamic Shapes,". The goal is to demonstrate a method for inferring 3D keypoint positions from multi-view silhouettes, particularly emphasizing the domain transfer from synthetic to real data using only 2D occupancy masks as observations. This is intended to create a 3D keypoint detector that is invariant to texture and illumination changes.
